C8 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Drags Mighty Porsche 911 Turbo, Someone Takes a Massive Beating – Twice
9 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Recently, we got all excited that, at long last, the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube finally went back to dwelling around their usual venue, which is Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey, a track that’s been around since it was established back in 1960.
Well, our joy was short-lived, as the videographer probably remembered they still had some cool action from the Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event that recently took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York. Usually, just like it happened at Pocono Raceway, the format over there was the 45-mph roll race variety because, obviously, their strip isn’t as long as the massive straight at Pocono.
But now it seems they also had some feisty drag races – or maybe this is a different edition dedicated to quarter-mile shenanigans . Anyway, enough musing about the formats and locations, come on, let’s meet the protagonists. First off, one of the heroes of this video is a pristine, white-shaded C8 Chevrolet Corvette identified as a hybrid performance E-Ray model.
In stock form, the model that shares many credentials with the Z06 but also adds an electrified package on top of the Stingray’s 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V8 makes out a combined output of 655 hp – and when it launched in 2023, it was also the first Corvette with all-wheel drive, not just the brand’s first performance hybrid.
Starting with the 2027 model year, it has been retired, though, as Chevrolet reintroduced the Grand Sport model and along came with it a Grand Sport X with 721 combined ponies to replace the E-Ray . Next to it lined up a silver Porsche 911 Turbo of the slightly older 991.2 variety, most likely. If we’re not mistaken, the German precision machine produced from 2016 through 2020 had a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six engine paired with a seven-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission and all-wheel drive, packing 540 hp, while the Turbo S jumped to 580 hp.
As one can see, both the E-Ray and 911 have all-wheel drive, but the Chevy has more power thanks to the hybrid setup – and it’s potentially heavier, also because of that. Now, let’s check out the video and see if the Porsche driver could negate the power difference on this unprepped surface. Well, as it turns out, as always, that’s easier said than done – the initial skirmish revealed the C8 was a handful for the 911 as it got beaten by at least a couple of car lengths.
Nevertheless, it seems the Porsche 911 driver wanted more and asked for a rematch, which was promptly granted. They switched lanes, as per tradition, and proceeded to hit the throttle once again. This time around, the impossible didn’t happen, and the C8 again won by about two car lengths…
